claims.text: The initial alloy is equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW.
The initial NbMoTaW microstructure is homogeneous and coarse.
A post-homogenization aging treatment can induce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoscale B2 precipitates in NbMoTaW.
Aging at 700–800 °C for 5–10 hours is an appropriate treatment window for producing the proposed B2 precipitates.
Optimization of aging parameters can keep the precipitates within a 10–20 nm size range and prevent overaging or coarsening.
The treatment will produce an inverted dual-phase structure with a continuous BCC matrix and discrete B2 precipitates.
Coherent nanoscale B2 precipitates create distributed obstacles to dislocation motion.
A continuous BCC matrix containing discrete B2 precipitates can improve room-temperature plasticity without sacrificing high strength.
The B2 precipitates will act as sinks for irradiation-generated point defects and helium atoms.
Defect and helium capture by B2 precipitates will reduce irradiation-induced amorphization.
Defect and helium capture by B2 precipitates will reduce helium blistering.
The proposed precipitates will suppress irradiation-enhanced precipitation.
Aged NbMoTaW will have greater room-temperature ductility than untreated NbMoTaW.
Aged NbMoTaW will have greater irradiation tolerance than untreated NbMoTaW.
The irradiation-tolerance improvement will apply from 20 to 700 °C.
The aged alloy will retain excellent mechanical strength up to approximately 1600 °C.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may coarsen or destabilize the nanoscale precipitates.
Precipitate coarsening under long-term thermal exposure or irradiation could degrade the proposed balance of ductility, strength, and irradiation tolerance.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as untreated, as-cast NbMoTaW, whereas aged samples receive homogenization before aging. Unless the control also receives the same homogenization and cooling history, the comparison changes both homogenization state and aging, so it does not isolate the proposed intervention.
